entries.topic: Israel: domestic surveillance law and episodes (Shin Bet Law s.11 'the Tool', COVID tracking 2020-21, police Pegasus affair 2022, biometric database, camera-hacking emergency law, Privacy Protection Law Amendment 13)

claims.text: HCJ 26 April 2020 (petitions by ACRI, Adalah/Joint List, Journalists' Union, Ben Meir): the GSS Law 2002 does not let the government use the Shin Bet beyond national security; no authority for COVID surveillance of citizens without legislation; first recognised limit on Shin Bet powers; interim continuation allowed

Netanyahu approved Shin Bet tracking in March 2020 by emergency regulation bypassing the Knesset; court required Knesset legislation and journalists' protection; court: 'a suitable alternative, compatible with the principles of privacy, must be found'

Knesset law (July 2020): government may order Shin Bet location tracking of contacts of confirmed cases in 21-day orders, only when more than 200 new cases a day, approved by a Knesset committee; appeal to Health Ministry within 24 hours; Privacy Protection Authority opposed it ('egregiously violates' privacy); in force until January 2021

AP/ToI 1 Jan 2021: 'the Tool' collects metadata (location, browsing, calls and texts, not content) and per Yedioth has been used about two decades; Health Ministry: since July 2020, 950,000 quarantined via the tool, 46,000 found infected, vs ~900,000 / 63,000 by traditional tracing; IDI's Shwartz Altshuler estimated at least 100,000 wrongly quarantined; State Comptroller interim report Oct 2020: contact tracing significantly more effective and Shin Bet did not always delete data

HCJ ruling (7 justices, Hayut presiding; reported 3 March 2021) on ACRI, PHRI and Adalah petition: from 14 March 2021 tracking limited to people who refuse to cooperate with tracers; court strongly recommended ending it; Justice Baron dissented to stop immediately; enabling law expired 20 January 2021
Bennett government reinstated Shin Bet tracking for Omicron carriers (announced ~27 Nov 2021); four rights groups incl. ACRI petitioned; Health Ministry said use would be 'surgical'

Section 11 of the ISA (Shin Bet) Law lets the prime minister require telecom providers to transfer data, including communications data but not content; no ex ante judicial review; ISA director authorises use for up to six months, renewable; rules classified; oversight by AG and annual report to Knesset subcommittee; ACRI petition pending; Justice Ministry draft amendment published 11 Dec 2023

Calcalist (18 Jan 2022) alleged police used Pegasus without warrants against mayors, former officials and leaders of protests against Netanyahu; Public Security Minister Barlev: no hacking 'without the approval of a judge'; AG, State Comptroller and police opened inquiries

Marari interim report 21 Feb 2022: 'no indication' police infected phones of anyone on the published list without a court order; police hold a Pegasus licence and another tool; three named people had hacking orders, two targeted, one hacked; Sa'ar: report 'incorrect', no need for state commission; Calcalist said it would re-examine

Marari further findings Aug 2022: no use without judicial order found, but police collected information beyond what warrants covered, a 'violation of authority'; ACRI cited 'major failures' and urged a bar until legislation

Biometric database law 2009 began with voluntary pilot; Knesset made it permanent (reported 7 March 2017): facial image mandatory for ID/passport; fingerprints stored unless applicant opts out (opt-out gets 5-year documents); no fingerprints for under-16s; police barred until Knesset regulations

Oct 2023 emergency regulations (IDF 14 Oct, Shin Bet 17 Oct) allowed hacking computers running stationary cameras without owner's knowledge or court order; reporting monthly to Knesset committee and AG, confidential; no court review or Privacy Protection Authority role

Knesset passed 13-4 on 25 June 2025 a six-month extension to 31 December 2025 of the IDF/Shin Bet authority to covertly access civilian security cameras, 'in light of the continuation of the fighting'

Amendment 13 to the Protection of Privacy Law 5741-1981 took effect 14 August 2025: privacy officers, data-broker rules, broader sensitive data, administrative fines and orders for the Privacy Protection Authority

Basic Law: Human Dignity and Liberty (1992) s.7(a): 'All persons have the right to privacy and to intimacy'; Wiretap Law 5739-1979 requires a district court president's warrant (up to 3 months, renewable); 2007 Criminal Procedure (Telecommunications Data) law lets police obtain metadata by court order, or without for 24 hours in some circumstances

entries.topic: United States: FISA, Section 702 over time and its 2026 lapse, wiretap reports, IRS-ICE data sharing, PCLOB

claims.text: Senate created the Church Committee 27 Jan 1975 (82-4); it documented COINTELPRO and NSA's SHAMROCK and MINARET; final report 29 Apr 1976: 'Intelligence agencies have undermined the constitutional rights of citizens'; led to the Senate Intelligence Committee (1976) and FISA (1978), which created the FISA Court

Guardian revealed the FISC Verizon call-records order in June 2013; Second Circuit (7 May 2015, ACLU v. Clapper) held the bulk telephone metadata program 'exceeds the scope of what Congress has authorized' under Section 215; USA FREEDOM Act passed 2 June 2015 restricting such collection
ODNI's first transparency report (June 2014) counted 89,138 Section 702 targets for 2013; 'targets' include groups and facilities
FBI ran nearly 3.4 million US person queries of 702 data in 2021 (a query may include many terms; ~1.9m terms related to potential victims); over 200,000 702 targets in 2021

ODNI ASTR (April 2026): 702 targets 268,590 (2023), 291,824 (2024), 349,823 (2025); FBI US person queries 57,094 (Dec22-Nov23), 5,518 (Dec23-Nov24), 7,413 (Dec24-Nov25); Title I/III and 703/704 targets 759, 602, 606
April 2026: House failed to pass a five-year or 18-month 702 renewal; 10-day extension to 30 April; nearly 350,000 targets; dispute over court approval before agents review Americans' data
30 April 2026: House voted 261-111 for a six-week extension to 12 June
Section 702 expired at midnight 12 June 2026 without renewal; EFF ties the lapse to the dispute over the nomination of Bill Pulte as DNI after Tulsi Gabbard resigned

Brennan Center (22 Sep 2026): FISC approved certifications 17 March 2026, valid until 17 March 2027; collection continues under them despite the lapse; government reportedly argued for renewal by November 2026
US Courts Wiretap Report 2025: 1,735 wiretaps authorized (873 federal, 862 state), down 24% from 2024 and 58% from 4,148 in 2015; narcotics 51% of applications

Treasury-DHS data-sharing agreement signed April 2025 (Bessent, Noem); ICE requested ~1.28m names; IRS verified ~47,000; DC Circuit panel (Edwards) 24 Feb 2026 declined to block sharing in the Centro de Trabajadores Unidos case

Judge Kollar-Kotelly (D.D.C.) stayed the IRS-ICE agreement Nov 2025 and in Feb 2026 found the IRS broke the law 'approximately 42,695 times'; DC Circuit (Pillard, unanimous) on 8 Sep 2026 affirmed the block in the Center for Taxpayer Rights case
Trump removed PCLOB Democrats LeBlanc and Felten in 2025, leaving the board sub-quorum; Judge Walton ruled 21 May 2025 the removals unlawful; White House expected 'ultimate victory'

claims.text: ISA Law s.11: classified reports quarterly to the attorney general and prime minister and annually to the Knesset Intelligence and Secret Services Subcommittee; 'the Tool' is the ISA communications metadata database; ACRI petition pending as of 21 March 2024.

Wiretap Law expanded in 1995 to mobile phones, computer communications and email; Israel has no statutory mandatory retention period for ISPs/telecoms; 'Shin Bet's "The Tool" effectively operates as a state-run retention system'.

Marari team included two former Shin Bet officials; former police commissioner Roni Alsheich had denied police access to Pegasus; Sa'ar: report 'incorrect and certainly not accurate', no need for state commission; interim report published 21 Feb 2022.

Government approved 15 July 2026 Shin Bet role vs crime in Arab communities; Netanyahu: 'We won't accept a situation of violence, extortion and murder on the streets'; ACRI: exceeds Shin Bet authority, organised crime in the Jewish community handled by police with regular tools; Abraham Initiatives: 'Crime is not terror'; Mossawa: diverts development funds.
Barlev (Jan 2022): 'there is no practice of wiretapping or hacking into devices by the Israel Police without the approval of a judge'.

EFF: 702 expired at midnight 12 June 2026; EFF credits Trump's nomination of Bill Pulte (FHFA director) as DNI, replacing Tulsi Gabbard who had announced her resignation the previous month, as the trigger; Senate Democrats then refused to move their reauthorisation bill and the House refused a short-term renewal.

AP Feb 2026: the administration argued the IRS-ICE agreement 'helps carry out President Donald Trump's agenda to secure U.S. borders'; AG Pam Bondi called the D.C. Circuit ruling (Edwards, 24 Feb 2026) a 'crucial victory'.
NPR 17 Apr 2026: Section 702 set to expire Monday 20 April 2026; House votes on five-year and the 18-month renewal Trump demanded failed; 10-day extension to 30 April.
